Replay

Inspecting a saved gameplay recording

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Godot controlsFile selection and bounds

Playback(State, Input, Event) loads a portable recording, verifies it once, and provides a presentation cursor over copied expected frames. Seeking and playback do not execute the simulation or deliver old events. The original game stays independent until its owner explicitly accepts a selected frame as a new branch.

Odin
player: d.Playback(World, Input, Event)
defer d.playback_destroy(&player)
loaded := d.playback_load(&player, bytes, identity, model)
if loaded.accepted {
    frame, ok := d.playback_read(&player)
    d.playback_seek(&player, player.recording.base.tick)
    d.playback_play(&player, true)
    d.playback_advance(&player, render_dt)
    // Paint copied frames. Do not send the recording's old events to effects.
}

A successful load starts paused at the first recorded frame. A state/event mismatch is accepted for inspection, starts at its first divergent tick, and keeps an owned Audit_Capture plus report text. verification distinguishes agreement from divergence; accepting a file is not a claim that it reproduces correctly. Malformed files, context/type mismatch, model-invalid values and aborted replay steps reject replacement, preserving the old recording, report and cursor.

Playback shows the recorded expected state, including at a mismatch. The report compares expected and replayed values. Full replay of the loaded window occurs only during load; the cursor never simulates or emits effects. Playback ends at the recorded head, and Play at the end restarts at its beginning. A zero-step recording remains stopped. Seek validates u64 ticks without converting absolute ticks to floating point. Invalid/nonfinite elapsed time does nothing; a render stall contributes at most 250 ms. Large elapsed steps skip intermediate visual frames in constant time, retaining the fractional tick between frames.

The owner and its recording/capture allocations must not be copied. Destroy before its owner leaves scope. Imported immutable asset identifiers still need the application's matching assets, just as in the recording contract.

Godot controls#

Debug_Playback(State, Input, Event) provides Open recording, a native or browser file chooser, Play/Pause, a relative-tick slider, Details, Return to game, and Continue from recording. It returns commands; the application owns its clock, input buffering, rendering and branch operation.

Odin
debuggd.debug_playback_init(&viewer, owner)
action := debuggd.debug_playback_frame(&viewer, identity, model, render_dt)
switch action {
case .Enter: // Save previous pause, pause the local clock, clear device edges.
case .Leave: // Restore previous pause and gate held input until released.
case .Branch:
    frame, ok := debuggd.debug_playback_read(&viewer)
    // Copy first. If accepted, initialize a new local timeline/presentation epoch
    // at frame.tick, then end playback. Never replay the file's historical effects.
case .None:
}
frame, showing := debuggd.debug_playback_read(&viewer)
// Paint frame while showing. While owns_pause but no frame is loaded, keep the
// original world paused and visible while the chooser is pending.
debuggd.debug_playback_end(&viewer)     // Explicit reset; owner restores its clock.
debuggd.debug_playback_destroy(&viewer) // Disconnect callbacks and release imports.

Keep the widget at a stable address until destroy. owns_pause covers both file selection and loaded playback. A canceled/failed first import releases that pause; a failed replacement keeps the old loaded view. Opening a replacement pauses its playback cursor. The application can read loads, rejections and last_load for diagnostics. Continue is an explicit branch from the displayed expected frame, including when the report shows a reproducibility mismatch. It does not repair that mismatch or change the imported archive.

Hello enables this alongside REPLAY_DEBUG=1. Entering the viewer ends a local history inspection, preserves its prior pause, and temporarily hides the live history/audit controls. Return restores the original game; Continue resets from the selected complete frame under a fresh local presentation epoch. Held gameplay input remains suppressed until released. Restart closes loaded/pending playback. No Session/Room/P2P runner or network authority is modified.

File selection and bounds#

File_Import is the stable owner for a bounded asynchronous selection. Native Godot uses its filesystem dialog, clamped to the parent window so its buttons remain reachable in Hello's 640×360 viewport. The .rplrec filter helps selection; codec checks still decide whether a file is valid. Native file bytes are read only after selection and are bounded before allocation.

Chrome uses an ordinary file input and checks size before File.arrayBuffer(). Each import has an ID; closing it discards the job, removes its DOM input and fences late completions. At most eight browser selections can exist at once. Cancellation, failed reads, zero/oversized files and byte-length changes terminate the request. Return to game can also cancel a pending selection. Teardown clears both pending jobs and callbacks. No upload to a server occurs.

Files retain the recording codec's 16 MiB limit and content/build/schema checks. Verification runs synchronously on load and can take time for a large world/window. This is an opt-in local developer workflow. It is not continuous recording, multi-window assembly, an editable imported timeline, movie export, or network recovery. To edit an imported frame in Hello, Continue from it, then use the local history field editor.

Run the native/Chrome acceptance to test real file selection, presentation, rejection, pause restoration and branching.
